text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The ruling coalition and right-wing opposition reached a "ceasefire" in a conflict over customs tariffs, under which the bill has been postponed to August.
- President of the Bank of Estonia Vahur Kraft warned against attempts to gain control of the central bank and assured again that the currency will not be devalued.
- Germany turned over to Estonia the first minesweeper of a promised two vessels.
- President Lennart Meri held the traditional reception for the best university and secondary school graduates.
- Tallinn district court rejected an appeal by retired general Aleksander Einseln for compensation for "moral harm" caused by his detention by the security police.
- The Migration Fund will pay emigrants from Estonia an extra summer support during the active migration period in summer. The extra sum is 1,000 kroons.
- Priit Saksing, chairman of northeastern Sillamae town council, intends to resign due to heart troubles.
- Parliament will debate six draft laws on European integration in the summer.
- The Development Party was officially registered yesterday. The party split away from the Centre Party a year ago and has since existed unofficially.

- An Estonian-US-Finnish team of researchers studied veterans of the nuclear clean up in Chernobyl and decided that the mens' main problems of the men were psychological and that radiation doses were quite light.
- Most articles were dedicated to the fifth anniversary of the Estonian national currency.
